clue.text: Morse upset by new lecture

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the detective's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse is put out by a fresh telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse, the TV detective, is anagram fodder here: 'upset' shuffles his name to SERMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a moral talk or reprimand, so a lecture in the scolding sense.

clue.text: Keep calm in stable, working

parts.note: steady means stable, not wobbling
on means operating, working, as of a machine

explanation.surface: Advice to stay composed while busy in the stables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a horse's stable but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady on is an exclamation urging someone to calm down.

clue.text: Drive off on East course

parts.note: to rout an enemy is to drive it off in defeat

explanation.surface: Instructions to drive away eastward along a path.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a way or path taken, a course.

clue.text: Leader of team employed by small company brought in work for ink producer

indicators.note: brought in means inserted into the word for a work

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially a musical composition

indicators.note: being employed by a company puts the letter inside the company's word

parts.note: Co is the short form of company

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of team

explanation.surface: A firm takes on a team leader to make printer's ink.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested insertions: 'employed by' and 'brought in' each put one piece inside another, making CTO first.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus squirts a cloud of ink to escape predators.

clue.text: Team full of power beginning to respect spinner

indicators.note: the team's word is filled with the letter for power, so it holds it inside

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
P is the physics abbreviation for power

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken here from respect

explanation.surface: A cricket team packed with strength starts to earn respect for its spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts P inside SIDE to make SPIDE; R comes from 'beginning to respect'. 'spinner' suggests a cricket bowler but means a web-spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins silk webs, so it is a spinner.

clue.text: The old man is on trial, unfortunately biased

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad stands trial and the judge, sadly, is prejudiced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns TRIAL into RTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Partial means favouring one side, prejudiced.

clue.text: Southern couple, during performance, lost heart

indicators.note: during means within, so these letters sit inside the word for performance

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A couple from the South lose their nerve mid-show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' signals the insertion; 'lost heart' looks like part of the wordplay (losing a middle letter) but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, to become disheartened.

clue.text: Go for a long walk with English novelist, right to the top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the front, so the letter moves to the start

parts.note: Eric Ambler was an English writer of spy thrillers

explanation.surface: Hiking with a writer, keeping to the right up to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the top' moves the final R of AMBLER to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramble is a leisurely walk in the countryside, and to ramble is to take one.

clue.text: Victim at heart of sincere denial

indicators.note: at the heart of means placed in the middle of the other word

parts.note: real feelings are sincere ones
a butt of jokes is their victim or target

explanation.surface: A wronged person at the centre of a heartfelt denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart of' puts BUTT in the middle of REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a contradiction or refutation of a claim, i.e. a denial.

clue.text: Plant, most unconfined, abundant

parts.note: loosest means least tied up, most free
rife means widespread, abundant

explanation.surface: A plant growing freely and in profusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosestrife is a flowering waterside plant, such as purple loosestrife.

clue.text: Take it, heading off for start again

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and it is taken off here

parts.note: to presume is to take it (as given) that something is so

explanation.surface: An instruction to accept something, then set off afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the first letter P from PRESUME.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to begin again after a pause.

clue.text: Not wanting to work in Madrid, lecturing

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: Someone lazy while giving lectures in Madrid.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of 'Madrid' and the start of 'lecturing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle describes someone lazy or inactive, unwilling to work.

clue.text: Lucrative for female, I suggest

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for
to table a motion is to put it forward, to suggest it

explanation.surface: Someone proposing a money-making idea for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Profitable and lucrative both mean yielding money.

clue.text: Fervent preacher, powerful active type full of charm

parts.note: hot can mean strong or powerful, as in a hot favourite

indicators.note: the word for an active type is filled with the charm's word

parts.note: a goer is an energetic, lively person
a spell is a charm or incantation

explanation.surface: A passionate preacher described as a forceful, energetic and charming character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' signals the insertion; a goer is British slang for a lively, energetic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot gospeller is an evangelical, zealous preacher of the Gospel.

clue.text: Drive way out in rental, then break down

parts.note: go means energy or drive, as in full of go

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for rental

parts.note: hire means rental, as in car hire

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trip in a hire car that ends in a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles the way to AYW, which 'in' places in the rental. 'Drive' suggests a car but means energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To go haywire is to malfunction or go out of control, as machines do.

clue.text: A nun abroad, joined by associate every year

indicators.note: abroad can mean all over the place, scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: A nun overseas with a companion on a yearly trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' turns A NUN into ANNU.
explanation.definitionFit: Annually means once a year, yearly.

clue.text: Causing great sadness, direction blocking trial

indicators.note: one word blocking another sits across it, inside it

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial
a trend is a general direction of movement

explanation.surface: A sad sight: a decision that stops a court case going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' signals the insertion; 'direction' looks like a compass point but is a general tendency.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heart-rending is deeply distressing, causing grief.

clue.text: A further part of 'Candida'? No, 'The Rivals'

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A theatregoer asks for one more play: not Shaw's Candida but Sheridan's The Rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means one more, an additional one.

clue.text: Inspect former pit round area

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a mine is a pit

explanation.surface: Survey an old colliery around the district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the insertion, giving MAINE after the prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to inspect closely.

clue.text: Pay and display

definitions.meaning: an arrangement of items or a page design

explanation.definitionFit: To lay out cash is to spend it; a layout is the arrangement or display of something.

clue.text: Gay old eccentric prima donna, the subject of a legendary tale

definitions.text: the subject of a legendary tale

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a diva is a prima donna, a leading female opera singer

explanation.surface: A colourful, ageing opera star who is the stuff of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' makes LADYGO from GAY OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Godiva is said to have ridden naked through Coventry, a famous English legend.

clue.text: Go round almost all of French city

indicators.note: almost all of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France

explanation.surface: A sightseer touring nearly the whole of a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all of' drops the final S of TOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: To tour a place is to travel around it.

clue.text: Unenthusiastic in assembly over bringing in piano

indicators.note: bringing in means taking the letter inside
over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in the Diet of Japan
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A half-hearted parliament reluctantly admitting a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DIET into TEID; 'bringing in' puts P inside, giving TEPID.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid means lukewarm, so figuratively lacking enthusiasm.

clue.text: European refinement

definitions.meaning: a person from Poland is a European
elegance and sophistication of manner, as in social finish

explanation.definitionFit: Polish is the nationality of Poland, a European country; polish also means refined elegance.

clue.text: Exploit amazingly large survey

indicators.note: amazingly suggests astonishing disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of a remarkably big opinion study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' reads as a verb but is anagram fodder: 'amazingly' shuffles it to EXITPOL.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit poll surveys voters leaving polling stations about how they voted.

clue.text: Conjecture made by those people importing gold

indicators.note: importing means bringing something in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: they refers to those people
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Speculation by traders who bring in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'importing' signals the insertion; OR as gold is a heraldic convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition or idea not yet proven, so a conjecture.

clue.text: Lethal dose heartlessly given by deranged lady

indicators.note: without its heart the word keeps only its outer letters
deranged means disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deadly dose handed out callously by a mad woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' leaves DE from DOSE; 'deranged' turns LADY into ADLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly and lethal both mean able to kill.
